objective: Plan HolyAgent 0.4.0: minimal harness installation, native Codex/cloud support and task-proportional architecture across harnesses.
requirements: Plan 0.4.0 now while continuing authorized 0.3.4 development/release. This Intent is planning only; do not implement or release 0.4.0 until authorized.

User installer requirement verbatim: bunx holyagent setup pi|claude|codex (they should just install the correct holyagent extension/plugin and that's it). Design one published entry point with explicit harness adapters and minimal installation effects; installing a harness adapter must not silently choose models, rewrite unrelated settings, install optional capability stacks or change account/guardrail defaults.

User Codex requirement: context_management, try to disable as many non-beneficial wasteful features, as well as find every bit of optimization in codex and its caching. holyagent codex should be compatible with codex cloud. Verify actual supported local/cloud Codex extension, instructions, skills and configuration APIs before choosing adapters. Distinguish context-management/compaction, caching, model/effort routing and optional features; measure benefits and preserve useful capabilities and permission controls. Do not assume undocumented knobs or authenticated host provenance.

User architecture requirement: simplify HolyAgent agents. Move PR-stack behavior into a gh-pr-stack skill; stacking must not be the default HolyAgent workflow. When explicitly using that skill, lower the number of PRs in a stack by grouping coherent reviewable changes and avoiding ceremonial PR splits. Preserve independently necessary security/review/CI boundaries.

User clarification verbatim: sometimes root might do overly complex orchestration for simple tasks that don't need orchestration at all, the orchestration deepness and amount should match the task. Root may directly handle straightforward low-risk tasks; use the minimum useful delegation/coordination. Scale Intent/Assignment detail, workflow depth, parallelism, specialist count and review effort to complexity, independence, risk and user value. Avoid mandatory workflow creation and universal delegation for trivial requests. Complex multi-step releases still benefit from explicit state, bounded ownership and independent reviews.

User shared-change rule: every change that is not harness-specific must be applied to all supported harnesses, adapted to each. Plan shared behavior contracts, a supported-harness capability matrix, requirement/model-family translations, adapter conformance tests and an exception rule for genuinely harness-specific features. Distinguish native Codex harness support in0.4.0 from the existing Codex provider inside Pi in0.3.4.

Planning outputs: current-vs-target architecture; verified Codex local/cloud support and optimization inventory with sources; installer command contract and idempotence/scope/uninstall strategy; optional gh-pr-stack skill boundaries and grouping rules; proportional-orchestration decision guide; cross-harness change checklist/conformance tests; dependency-ordered implementation slices and release acceptance criteria.

Acceptance before implementation: do not select unsafe performance optimizations from speculative claims; document expected benefits, benchmark methods, privacy/approval implications and rollback. Preserve user settings. Avoid installing packages or changing security settings in this planning phase.

Fast-tier clarification (2026-11-13): primary budget target is $100 subscription plans, with a fast option for the $20 tier across EVERY provider and harness. The Claude fast-tier ROOT is Sonnet. GPT6.1Terra is the user's Codex fast-root example instead of Sol. Root preferences are distinct from specialist routing. Carry the0.3.4 profile/score contract into0.4.0 adapters, preserving account capability checks and explicit overrides. Optimize actual cost/context/latency without inventing benchmark scores.

Carry forward the0.3.4 task-baseline visual and performance cycle into every0.4.0 harness adapter: immutable original baseline before edits; every commit compared to original and previous; screenshots/real-use/video where supported; project design-system composition/motion/responsiveness checks; optimization objective/target established at task start, controlled complete relevant measurement and per-commit deltas/noise/regressions. This is part of the shared-harness contract and scales to task scope without ceremonial work on unrelated tasks.

Accepted planning decisions and sources: use thin native adapters over shared behavior contracts, not a universal Pi wrapper; setup installs only the matching artifact with explicit scope, idempotent ownership receipts, safe undo/conflict handling and no account/model/guardrail changes. Codex local plugin docs describe codex plugin marketplace add and trusted-project activation (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins); this does NOT establish Codex Cloud loading. Cloud activation and a real authorized smoke are explicit pre-implementation/claim gates. Context management and caching controls must be verified per host/account; measure useful benefit, preserve approvals, support rollback. Relevant sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/compaction and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching . Keep normal task behavior direct/minimally delegated; optional gh-pr-stack groups coherent reviewable changes, no default stack. Carry normal/fast profiles and role-specific overrides through adapter conformance tests.

Implementation order, when later authorized: (1) rebase on accepted0.3.4 APIs/profiles and resolve actual native/cloud interfaces; (2) shared proportional orchestration and optional-stack skill across current harnesses; (3) minimal published CLI/setup adapters with idempotent upgrade/conflict/undo; (4) native Codex local/cloud loading and smoke tests; (5) measured context/cache/profile optimizations and cross-harness/OS conformance. Preserve the user's immutable visual/performance task baseline and per-commit original+previous comparison as acceptance criteria. No0.4.0 code, branch, PR or installation has been created.
